clue.text: A little stone work by a mathematician

definitions.meaning: in medicine and in Latin the word names a small stone, such as one formed in the kidney
the branch of mathematics dealing with differentiation and integration

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for a pebble gave its name both to a stony concretion in the body and, via counting pebbles, to a branch of mathematics.

clue.text: Even carpet knights have experienced this sword-play

definitions.text: Even carpet knights have experienced this sword-play

parts.words: Even carpet knights have experienced this sword-play
parts.note: a carpet knight is a soldier who never saw battle, but even he received the sword's touch on the shoulder when knighted

explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial tap on the shoulder with a sword that confers knighthood.

clue.text: His " pearls " are of little price

definitions.text: His " pearls " are of little price

parts.words: His " pearls " are of little price
parts.note: London street traders' pearly suits are covered in cheap pearl buttons, and the traders sell cheaply too

explanation.walkthrough: London street traders' kings and queens wear 'pearly' suits sewn with buttons, unlike the biblical pearl of great price.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrow-boy selling fruit and vegetables in London's streets, of the pearly king tradition.

clue.text: No honest settler, he's off — like the wind?

definitions.meaning: one who levants, absconding without settling debts
a strong easterly wind in the western Mediterranean

explanation.definitionFit: A bolter who runs off leaving debts unpaid, and also a strong easterly blowing from the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Sid appears madly busy without financial aid

indicators.note: the rearranged letters stand outside, surrounding the name
acting madly, these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the anagram fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Sid seems frantically occupied, with no money to help him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' rearranges BUSY into SUBY, and 'without' (meaning outside) wraps it around SID.
explanation.definitionFit: A grant of money, typically from government, to support an undertaking.

clue.text: Learning his multiplication initially by division

parts.note: Sc is the abbreviation for science, from Latin for knowledge
taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter only of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A schoolchild's arithmetic lessons, starting with times tables and moving on to sums of sharing.
explanation.definitionFit: A split within a group, especially a church, into opposing factions.

clue.text: One of Hook's men goes up East German river

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
the Ems flows through north-west Germany

explanation.surface: A pirate travels upstream on a river in eastern Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes up' turns E plus EMS, EEMS, upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Hook's bosun in Barrie's Peter Pan is a pirate of this name.

clue.text: Case of Nine Cats maybe

indicators.note: suggests the letters could form something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A display box holding nine cats, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: An example or occurrence, as in 'in this case'.

clue.text: Rare — non-garden, too ?

parts.note: the prefix un- does the same negating job as non-
from the phrase 'common or garden', meaning ordinary

explanation.surface: A rare plant is described as being not from the garden either.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common or garden' is a British phrase for ordinary, so 'garden' stands for COMMON.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seldom met with is out of the ordinary; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Winners of top honours

parts.note: in card games the highest cards in each suit, which take tricks, are the top honours

explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the highest-ranking honour cards win tricks, so these are the trick-winners among the top honours.

clue.text: If ten pints harm a change in port is indicated

indicators.note: these letters signal a different word, read as a rearrangement of the fodder before it

explanation.surface: Drunkenness after ten pints is blamed for a ship's reassignment in harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is indicated' tells you to rearrange TEN PINTS HARM; 'If' is a link word. The OCR read 'ten' as 'ton'.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving cargo or passengers from one vessel to another, typically at a port, is a change of ship.

clue.text: Dramatic Salvationist

parts.note: the heroine of a Shaw play, an officer in the Salvation Army

explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's play is named for its heroine, an officer of the Salvation Army.

clue.text: Bird that copies a fashion

definitions.meaning: a tropical bird known for mimicking speech
one that imitates, repeating what others do or say without thought

explanation.definitionFit: The bird famous for mimicry gave its name to any imitator who repeats others mechanically.

clue.text: Jo's bottle

parts.note: the name Jo is the first half of the name John, so it is a half-John

explanation.walkthrough: DEMI means half, and Jo is half of the letters of John: a reverse clue, the answer read as wordplay giving the clue word.
explanation.definitionFit: A large narrow-necked bottle, often wicker-covered, used for wine or home brewing.

clue.text: Writing about one more variety of days gone by

indicators.note: the manuscript letters go around the rest, as if surrounding it

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author writes about another kind of bygone era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges I and MORE into EMOIR, and 'about' puts that inside MS.
explanation.definitionFit: Recollections written by someone of their own past are an account of the days gone by.

clue.text: Businessman whose service is overseas

definitions.meaning: the ... navy, also called the ... service, sails abroad

explanation.definitionFit: A wholesale trader, and the commercial fleet carrying goods abroad is called the merchant service.

clue.text: The housing row

parts.note: a row that houses people, rather than a quarrel about housing

explanation.definitionFit: A continuous row of joined houses sharing side walls is called by this name in Britain.

clue.text: Rosalind in her last speech

parts.note: in As You Like It, Rosalind delivers the closing address to the audience after the play ends

explanation.definitionFit: A closing speech addressed to the audience, spoken by Rosalind at the end of As You Like It.

clue.text: There's many a layer with the Italian and French forms of material

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
a hen is a bird that lays eggs
il is Italian for 'the'
le is the French form of 'the'

explanation.surface: Many hens, with Italian and French bloodlines, and the fabric they are bred on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Italian and French forms' gives the definite article in each language, IL and LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A velvety tufted yarn or fabric, used for upholstery and soft furnishings.

clue.text: " Inane " is another 'way of putting it

definitions.text: " Inane " is another 'way of putting it

indicators.note: the same letters put another way, that is rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that 'inane' is simply a synonym for something else.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange INANE IS; the whole clue also defines the answer, since a silly thing is inane put another way.
explanation.definitionFit: The rearranged word is a synonym of inane, meaning foolish or silly.

clue.text: Tintinnabulations of Goldilocks ?

parts.note: bell-ringing reads as small rings, and the fairytale girl's golden hair is curled

explanation.definitionFit: Corkscrew curls of hair, read as little peals of bells, belong to the golden-haired girl.

clue.text: Roman standards are below par of course

definitions.meaning: the legions of Rome carried eagle figures as standards
on a golf course, a score two under par on a hole

explanation.definitionFit: The bird emblems of Rome's legions, and in golf scores of two strokes under par.

clue.text: She is a Babylonian idol

parts.note: taken as written
Bel was a god worshipped in Babylon

explanation.surface: A woman is described as a pagan statue from ancient Babylon.
explanation.walkthrough: Bel is the Babylonian god mocked in the Apocrypha's Bel and the Dragon.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so a female person referred to as 'she'.

clue.text: Wherein an aspirate at length is disastrously dropped

definitions.text: Wherein an aspirate at length is disastrously dropped

parts.words: Wherein an aspirate at length is disastrously dropped
parts.note: the letter H, an aspirate, is the chemical symbol of an element; spelt at length it names the weapon's fuel, and the weapon is dropped with disastrous effect

explanation.walkthrough: Dropping an aspirate means not pronouncing H; here the H, written out as its element, is literally dropped from a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermonuclear weapon released from an aircraft, getting its power from fusion of the lightest element.

clue.text: Low-down drug

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for inside information, and also for an illegal narcotic.

clue.text: Aunt is fairly decapitated by a friend

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter goes

parts.note: an Aunt Sally is the wooden figure thrown at in a fairground game

explanation.surface: An aunt's head is knocked off by a pal, at a fair.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aunt Sally is a British fairground target at which sticks are thrown; 'decapitated' removes its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter on one's side, a companion or partner.

clue.text: G.K.C. brand brandy in Notting Hill ?

definitions.text: G.K.C. brand brandy in Notting Hill ?

parts.words: G.K.C. brand brandy in Notting Hill ?
parts.note: G.K. Chesterton wrote a novel naming an emperor's title after a London district; the emperor is also a brand of brandy

explanation.walkthrough: Chesterton's novel is The Napoleon of Notting Hill; Notting Hill is a district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The French emperor's name is given to a grade of cognac and to the hero of Chesterton's novel.

clue.text: Being ennobled gets one places in New York

definitions.meaning: raised in rank, as to the peerage

definitions.text: gets one places in New York
definitions.meaning: the overhead railway in New York, the 'El', carried passengers around the city

explanation.definitionFit: Raised to a higher rank, and also the name of New York's overhead railway that took riders about town.
